people.line: Faultless from birth, and built for exactly this. He sees what tongue cannot tell and asks to die.
The Grail's original hero, demoted to a companion once Galahad exists. In Wolfram he is the one who succeeds, and the difference is the whole argument.
The only one who comes home. Not a virgin, not faultless — the man who made a hard choice and paid for it, and went back to a doomed court and stayed.
Gets further than anyone else who fails: as far as the chamber door, where he is struck down and lies twenty-four days, one for each year of the love.
Told in a paragraph that he will find nothing, because he has not confessed in years and does not intend to. He accepts it and rides home, killing eighteen companions on the way.
Gives all her blood to cure a stranger and dies of it. Her body reaches the Grail city ahead of the knights. The text never gives her a name.
Not a quester but the reason for the quest. In Wolfram he is cured when somebody finally asks what is wrong with him.
